approach: Root cause (read in crates/athena-core/src/checks.rs:373-419): `failure_section`, the one place a failed check's output is chosen for storage, finds the failing section only through runner markers (`is_runner_marker`, 354) and cuts cleanup only at a cleanup HEADER (`is_cleanup_line`, 345: "Post job cleanup", "Post Run ", "Cleaning up orphan processes"). A log with no marker, such as a cancelled, timed-out or "did not finish" shard, or a cleanup block whose header is missing or not matched, falls through to a plain tail. That tail is the git credential-removal lines, "Cleaning up orphan processes" and the Node.js warning. Nothing tells the reader that no failing section existed. The fix stays in checks.rs. (1) `is_cleanup_line` also recognises cleanup by content, in this one function. (2) A new cut rule finds where the trailing cleanup block starts: the first cleanup line at or after the anchor whose suffix is mostly cleanup or blank lines. (3) A body left empty returns an explicit note. (4) A new `ci_failure_section` wrapper prepends a "no failing test section found" note when the log has no runner marker. `detail_from_job_logs` (gh/client.rs:344) calls the wrapper for each per-shard log. `with_failure_detail` (checks.rs:424, used by routing.rs:287), the local run (checks.rs:618) and `CheckFailure::of` (send_back.rs:297) all go through `failure_section`, so every producer of a failed record is covered. No record shape, admission or gate code changes.

decisions.choice: Extend `is_cleanup_line` in checks.rs to match content forms as well as headers: lines starting `/usr/bin/git `, `[command]/usr/bin/git`, `Temporarily overriding HOME`, `Adding repository directory to the temporary git global config`, `Removing HTTP extra header`, `Removing includeIf`, `Complete job`, `Evaluate and set job outputs`, `##[warning]Node.js`, plus `##[group]`/`##[endgroup]`. Add a private `cleanup_start(lines, anchor)` that applies the density rule. Both live in checks.rs and nothing is copied elsewhere.
decisions.reason: Criterion 4 wants one recogniser. The brief's log shape has git credential-removal lines before 'Cleaning up orphan processes' and a Node warning after it. The current cut at the header leaves the git lines (checks.rs:380-392), so the base fails criterion 1. The density rule (the suffix from the candidate must be at least half cleanup or blank lines) stops one stray content-matching line, for example a Node warning near the start of a log with no marker (anchor 0), from cutting the whole log.

rejected.option: Strip only the maximal run of recognised lines from the end of the log
rejected.why: The real block holds unrecognised lines such as `http.https://github.com/.extraheader` and `fatal:` lines. One unrecognised line would stop the strip and leave earlier cleanup lines.

rejected.option: A second `is_cleanup_content` function in gh/client.rs or send_back.rs
rejected.why: Criterion 4 forbids a second copy, and local runs would not get it.

rejected.option: A refusal rule rejecting a failed check record that has no test names
rejected.why: The request prefers giving the storing stage the information. Nothing is refused, so 0% of past accepted readings are newly refused.

decisions.choice: `failure_section` returns a fixed note, `NO_OUTPUT_NOTE`, when removing cleanup leaves nothing. A new `pub fn ci_failure_section` calls `failure_section` and puts `NO_TEST_SECTION_NOTE` first when the log has no runner marker. `detail_from_job_logs` calls it for each readable shard log. The note is not added in `failure_section` itself.
decisions.reason: `failure_section` also serves local fmt, clippy and command checks, whose output legitimately has no test section. Existing test `failure_section_without_marker_or_cleanup_is_the_old_tail` (checks.rs:892) pins that the plain tail stays. Only a CI test-shard log should say 'no failing test section'. `with_failure_detail` re-applies `failure_section` to a tail that already carries the note. Because it calls the unwrapped function, no second note is added and the note is not cleanup text, so it survives.

rejected.option: Add the note inside `failure_section` for every marker-less log
rejected.why: It would rewrite local clippy and fmt output and break the pinned old-tail test.
It would miss the multi-shard layout built in client.rs, and a tail with the `failing units:` prefix would be handled twice.

decisions.choice: `CheckFailure::of` runs `failure_section(&run.output_tail, FAILED_TAIL_LINES, FAILED_TAIL_BYTES)` before taking the 3000-byte tail. routing.rs gets a test only, with no production edit.
decisions.reason: This keeps the send-back clean for a run whose stored tail was recorded before the fix or came from another source. `failure_section` is idempotent on already-cleaned text. routing.rs:276-293 already sends reused red `test` runs through `with_failure_detail`, so it needs only a test showing the reused path stays clean.

rejected.option: Cut the send-back tail differently, to keep the section start when the section exceeds 3000 bytes
rejected.why: That is a separate length question and not this root cause. It is listed as a risk.

steps: In checks.rs, extend `is_cleanup_line` to match the content forms listed in decisions plus the existing headers. Add private `cleanup_start(lines: &[&str], anchor: usize) -> Option<usize>`: the first index i >= anchor with `is_cleanup_line(lines[i])` where, counting lines from i to the end, cleanup-or-blank lines are at least half. Keep the existing `c > 0` meaning by handling `Some(0)` as an empty body.

In `failure_section`, replace the inline `position(...)` (checks.rs:380-384) with `cleanup_start`. After the cut, drop trailing blank lines. When the body is empty or only whitespace, return `NO_OUTPUT_NOTE`. Leave the marker, window and jump logic (393-418) unchanged.

Add the consts `NO_OUTPUT_NOTE` ('(no output was kept: the log held only runner cleanup text)') and `NO_TEST_SECTION_NOTE` ('(no failing test section was found in this log; the last lines before runner cleanup follow)'). Add `pub fn ci_failure_section(text, max_lines, max_bytes) -> String`, which calls `failure_section` and prepends the note when no line satisfies `is_runner_marker` and the section is not `NO_OUTPUT_NOTE`. Add the checks.rs tests from demonstrations 1 and 3(a)(b), and rewrite the test at checks.rs:933.

In gh/client.rs, change the call at line 344 to `crate::checks::ci_failure_section`, correct the doc comment at 286-295 (the tail now holds the failing section or a note, with no cleanup text), and add `#[cfg(test)] mod detail_tests` with the two tests of demonstration 2.

In send_back.rs, change `CheckFailure::of` to `tail: crate::checks::tail(&crate::checks::failure_section(&run.output_tail, FAILED_TAIL_LINES, FAILED_TAIL_BYTES), CHECK_FAILURE_TAIL_BYTES)`. Add the `with_failure_detail_tail_is_clean_in_the_send_back` test to `check_failure_tests`.
In routing.rs's tests module, add `with_failure_detail_routing_a_red_run_stores_no_cleanup` using the `Detailed` stub with a cleanup-bearing `FailureDetail`.
Add the CHANGELOG.md `### Fixed` entry under `## [Unreleased]` (insert after the entry at line 23, before `### Added` at line 25).
Run `cargo fmt --all`, `cargo clippy --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings` and `cargo test --locked`, and fix any failure in the touched tests.

risks.risk: The cleanup recognisers are a list of known strings. A new runner cleanup form, or an unrecognised line inside the block, leaves some cleanup text in the record. The note still says when no test section was found.
risks.mitigation: The content set is wide: git, Node, 'Complete job' and the three header forms. The density rule tolerates some unrecognised lines in the block, and the tests cover the log shape from the failed jobs. The CHANGELOG says the match is by known text, and residual noise is not claimed to be zero.

risks.risk: The density rule or the content forms cut a real failing section, for example test output that starts with `/usr/bin/git ` after the last marker.
risks.mitigation: The cut starts at the anchor (the last runner marker or `##[error]`) and needs a mostly-cleanup suffix. Existing tests at checks.rs:857-930 and gh/tests.rs:726-772 must still pass. A new test keeps a stray cleanup-looking line before the section.

risks.risk: The send-back keeps only the last 3000 bytes of a section that may be up to 64 KB, so a long section can lose its `failures:` header.
risks.mitigation: This is not caused by cleanup text and is left unchanged. It is a separate request.

risks.risk: Stored records written before the change still hold cleanup text.
risks.mitigation: They are not rewritten. Only the send-back view re-cleans them.

demonstrations.method: Add `failure_section_drops_headerless_cleanup_block` to the tests module of checks.rs. The input is built inline: about 40 progress lines ('shard progress N'), then the git credential-removal lines (`/usr/bin/git config --local --unset-all http.https://github.com/.extraheader`, `Removing HTTP extra header`, `Removing includeIf ...`), then `Cleaning up orphan processes`, then `##[warning]Node.js 20 actions are deprecated`. There is no `Post job cleanup.` header, no runner marker and no `##[error]`. It calls `failure_section(&text, FAILED_TAIL_LINES, FAILED_TAIL_BYTES)`. The output must contain 'shard progress 39' and none of the git, `Removing`, `Cleaning up orphan`, `Node.js` strings. A second case of only cleanup lines must equal `NO_OUTPUT_NOTE`. The old test `failure_section_of_only_cleanup_is_the_whole_text` (checks.rs:933) is rewritten to expect the note. This is an update to an existing test.
demonstrations.observes: All failure_section tests pass. That includes the new headerless-cleanup test and the unchanged jump, wide-line, old-tail and marker-then-cleanup tests (checks.rs:857-936), so the density rule does not cut a real section.
demonstrations.fails_without: On the base tree the cut is at 'Cleaning up orphan processes' (checks.rs:380-384), which leaves the git credential-removal lines in the output, so the new test's assertions fail. The cleanup-only test fails too, because the base returns the whole text.
demonstrations.seam: The production entry point is `checks::failure_section` (pub, checks.rs:373). Its input is a plain `&str`, so no fake is needed. The existing in-file `mod tests` has the helpers `cleanup_text` and `failing_section_text`. The seam exists.

demonstrations.method: Add `mod detail_tests` in gh/client.rs, next to `origin_tests` at client.rs:1246. It calls the production `detail_from_job_logs` (client.rs:296) with a `Vec<(String, String, Option<String>)>` built inline. Case A: one job `test (shard 3)`, conclusion `cancelled`, log of progress lines then git removal, `Cleaning up orphan processes` and a Node warning, with no marker. Assert `output_tail` contains the progress lines and `NO_TEST_SECTION_NOTE`, contains no cleanup strings, and `failed_tests` is empty. Case B: a `failure` shard whose log has `== shard 1/6: athena-core --lib`, `failures:`, `    tests::a`, a `thread ... panicked at` line and `test result: FAILED`, followed by cleanup lines. Assert `failed_tests == ["athena_core tests::a"]` or the form `failed_test_names` gives, the output keeps the test name and the panicked line, and the note is absent.
demonstrations.observes: The new tests, named with the substring `detail_from_job_logs`, pass. The existing gh/tests.rs tests that drive the same function (job_log_parser_strips_stamps..., two_shards_each_keep_their_failing_section, cleanup_after_an_xtask_panic...) still pass. They do not contain that substring, so the verifier also runs `cargo test -p athena-core gh::`.
demonstrations.fails_without: On the base tree `NO_TEST_SECTION_NOTE` does not exist, and case A's output holds the git and Node cleanup lines, so the assertions fail.
demonstrations.seam: The production entry point is `gh::client::detail_from_job_logs` (pub). Its input is inline job tuples, with no host or fake. `plain_log_line` (client.rs:203) accepts unstamped lines. The module is added by plan step 4. The existing tests in gh/tests.rs are untouched, because that file is not a deliverable.

demonstrations.method: Name every criterion-3 test with `with_failure_detail`. (a) checks.rs: `with_failure_detail_drops_headerless_cleanup_from_the_stored_tail` builds a reused red run with the existing helpers `reused_failed` and `detail`, whose tail has a `failing units:` line, progress lines, then the cleanup lines. A passthrough redactor is injected. It asserts the stored `output_tail` has no cleanup strings, and that the units line stays first. (b) checks.rs: `with_failure_detail_and_local_run_never_store_cleanup` runs `run_script` (checks.rs:821) on a `sh_spec` script that prints failing-test lines, the git removal lines, `Cleaning up orphan processes` and a Node warning, then exits 1. It asserts the local `output_tail` has the test lines and none of the cleanup. (c) send_back.rs, in `check_failure_tests`: `with_failure_detail_tail_is_clean_in_the_send_back` takes a `CheckRun` whose `output_tail` still holds the cleanup lines, calls `CheckFailure::of`, and asserts `tail` has none of them, then calls `append_check_failures` and asserts the brief text has none. (d) routing.rs: `with_failure_detail_routing_a_red_run_stores_no_cleanup` uses the existing `Detailed` stub at routing.rs:565 with a cleanup-bearing `FailureDetail` and `run_routed_with_record`. It asserts the stored `test` run's `output_tail` has no cleanup.
demonstrations.observes: All four tests pass. Together they cover the reused-CI path (with_failure_detail through routing), the local run path (run_check) and the send-back view, so the property is shown on every producer of a failed record.
demonstrations.fails_without: On the base tree each of the four fails. The headerless git and Node lines survive `failure_section`, which both `with_failure_detail` and `run_check` call, and `CheckFailure::of` only takes a byte tail.
demonstrations.seam: The production entry points are `checks::with_failure_detail`, `checks::run_check` (via the existing `run_script` helper), `CheckFailure::of` and `append_check_failures`, and `routing::run_routed_with_record`. The fakes are the existing `Detailed` and `Local` stubs (routing.rs:520-590, injected as `&dyn CiSource` and `&dyn Exec`) and an inline redaction closure. All exist today.
